1.title: A Mill, a Donkey, and a Cat

paragraphs.text: Some people gathered in a graveyard.
The miller's three sons stood by the grave.
Their names were Francis, Batista, and Carabas.
"I'm glad he lived a nice long life."
Later the brothers went to the mill.
"He only owned this mill and a donkey."
And I'll make money grinding flour."
"Well, I'm taking the donkey," Batista said.
"I can use it to carry goods to the market."
"Let's go into business together," Francis said.
"I'll grind flour, and you take it to the market."
Batista shrugged. "Father didn't own anything else."
Just then a cat pounced on a mouse.
Francis grinned. "Carabas, you can have Puss."
Each morning Carabas worked in his garden.
Batista walked by with his donkey.
Suddenly an apple rolled down from the road.
The apple was red and shiny.
Then Carabas spotted a man with an apple cart.
The man thanked him. "You're very honest!"
He bought a small loaf of bread.
A man was playing a guitar.
"Did you hear the news?" a man asked.
"An ogre came down from the hills!"
Carabas gulped. "Where is the ogre now?"
He was going to lock his door too!
At home Carabas locked his door.
He fed Puss bits of bread.
"I wish I had more food for you."
It was a small bowl of soup.
He dipped some bread in it.
A chilly wind blew under the door.
Carabas put a blanket over the cat.
That night he tossed and turned in bed.
"Soon I will need more money," he thought.
The next morning Carabas worked in the garden.
Suddenly the cat's paw shot out.
That afternoon Carabas spotted Puss again.
"What is that cat doing now?" he thought.
The cat was at the garden shed.
With his back feet, he hung from the doorway.
Just then a mouse ran by.
"I wish Puss could catch food for me too!"
Carabas was in town, buying flour and salt.
The man waited as Carabas counted out coins.
A basket of dried fish sat on the table.
Carabas saw it and thought of Puss.
"How much for the dried fish?" he asked.
The man told him the price.
"That's too much money," Carabas thought. "Oh well."
He paid for the flour and salt and left.
"Puss is a great cat," Carabas thought.
"I want to do something nice for him."
Carabas ran back to the store.
Carabas had a long walk home.
He couldn't wait to give Puss the treat!
Later Puss ate his dried fish.
"I'm glad you like it," Carabas said.
After dinner Carabas counted his coins again.
Each day the pile grew smaller.
Puss jumped into his master's lap.
"That's not true, Master," Puss said suddenly.
Puss waved a paw. "Talking is easy."
"But how can you talk?" Carabas asked.
"I have a plan to help you."
"Puss is a very unusual cat," he thought.
"First I need a bag and some boots," Puss said.
Carabas looked at the coins on the table.
"I don't have much money," Carabas said.
The next day they went to the shoemaker.
"I need a pair of boots," Carabas said.
The shoemaker looked at Carabas' feet.
Then he told Carabas the price.
"Sir, the boots are for me," he said.
Puss shrugged. "It's not a big deal."
"I can make you a pair for a few coins."
"They'll be the fanciest boots in the kingdom!"
Puss had his new, fancy boots.
Puss smiled. "Master, I must look my best.
That is how a cat gets respect."
"I will be back later," he said.
"I have a plan, remember?" Puss said.
Outside, Puss got a carrot from the garden.
He dropped it into the bag.
Then he headed down the road.
Puss came to a meadow and stopped.
He put the bag on the ground.
Then he hid behind a bush and waited.
The rabbit stuck its nose in the bag.
Puss quickly tied up the bag.
"Master might like this rabbit for dinner," he said.
The king looked in a mirror.
He turned to the side and gasped.
"Sal, come in here!" the king cried.
"There's a hair on my robe," the king said.
The servant picked off the hair.
I can't have a hair on my robe!"
The king walked into the throne room and sat.
People were waiting to see him.
A servant let in one person at a time.
"Your Majesty, I need a job," she said.
Her hair fell in her face.
The king gave the woman a job.
He also gave her a hair tie.
"My neighbors are poor," the man said.
"Take some grain for your neighbors," the king said.
"Get this man a belt!" he shouted.
The king frowned as the man left.
A cat in fancy boots walked in!
The king looked at Puss' boots.
The king grinned. "I feel the same way!"
"I have a gift for you," Puss said.
He pulled the rabbit from the bag.
"It's from my master, the Duke of Carabas."
"Tell the duke I said thank you."
The next day Puss went to the forest.
He placed seeds in the bag.
Puss climbed up a tree and waited.
Two birds landed near the bag.
He pounced on the birds and caught them!
Puss returned to the castle with the birds.
He bowed. "A gift from the Duke of Carabas."
The king handed a gold coin to Puss.
"But the duke has everything he needs."
"Then he can buy something he doesn't need.
Just then Puss walked in with a gold coin.
Carabas gasped. "Where did you get that?"
Puss shrugged. "The king gave it to me."
Puss nodded. "He and I are friends."
Puss gave Carabas the gold coin.
Puss visited the king every day.
He brought a gift every day too.
A singer sang for the cat.
One day Puss and the king had lunch.
"Tell me about the duke," the king said.
Puss smiled. "The duke is honest and kind."
The king will see that he is poor!"
"My master is, um, very busy right now.
I'm sure you can meet him soon, though."
The king wanted to meet Carabas.
One day Puss visited the castle.
The king was taking a nap.
As Puss walked around, he heard music.
"Someone is playing a guitar," Puss thought.
Puss followed the sound through the castle.
Puss saw a young woman with a guitar.
Her fingers danced along its strings.
Puss was confused. "Who is your father?"
I was traveling and came home last night."
Puss bowed. "It's an honor to meet you.
She stood. "Come. Let's walk and talk.
Father and I were going to take a carriage ride.
Puss and Fiona walked and talked.
Soon the king found them outside.
"I'm sorry I fell asleep, Fiona," the king said.
"Let's take that carriage ride tomorrow morning."
A grin spread across the cat's face.
He heard a squawk and wings flapping.
Several birds flew off from his berry bushes.
They carried berries in their beaks.
"Birds are eating my berries," he thought.
"Puss gave me a gold coin," he thought.
"I'll use it for food—and some nets.
Then I can cover the berry bushes."
Later Puss found Carabas in the garden.
Carabas was placing nets over the berry bushes.
"I have a plan to change your life.
Carabas shook his head and laughed.
Puss told Carabas all about Fiona.
He didn't say she was a princess.
Carabas' pants and shirt had holes.
His shoes were still falling apart.
"First we must go shopping," Puss said.
"Where is the gold coin from the king?"
Carabas bit his lip. "I'm sorry, Puss.
I spent it on food and these nets.
But he had no money for new clothes.
Tomorrow Fiona will take a carriage ride.
"I told the king you're a rich duke," Puss said.
Puss waved a paw. "It's just a little lie."
"No, it's a big lie!" Carabas said.
Carabas folded his arms. "I will forget her."
But Puss still had a plan—a sneaky plan.
"Let's go swimming," Puss said the next morning.
Puss grinned. "I know a nice spot along the road."
Carabas and Puss went to the river.
Carabas took off his ripped clothes.
The king and Fiona were riding in their carriage.
Two men carried him out of the river.
Carabas gulped. It was the king!
"Guards!" the king said. "Ride to the castle.
Get dry clothes for the duke."
Soon they were back with dry clothing.
Carabas put on the fine clothes.
"Who is playing the guitar?" he asked.
Oh, what did you want to tell me?"
He was still listening to the music.
"What were you going to say?" the king asked.
Carabas shook his head. "It . . . it was nothing."
The king put his hand on Carabas' shoulder.
"My dear," the king said to Fiona.
"It is nice to meet you," Fiona said.
"My daughter and I are taking a ride.
"Puss can come too," the king said.
Carabas scratched his head. "I don't know."
"Fiona, your music is beautiful," he said.
She picked up her guitar and played.
Meanwhile Puss ran far ahead of the carriage.
Puss saw men cutting hay in a meadow.
"The king will be coming along soon.
Tell him the Duke of Carabas owns this meadow."
"We won't lie to the king," another said.
Puss showed his claws. "Yes, you will!"
The carriage soon passed the meadow.
"Who owns this meadow?" the king asked.
"The Duke of Carabas owns it," one man said.
Carabas was confused, but he stayed quiet.
"Hey there!" Puss called to some workers.
One man looked up in surprise. "Yes?"
"Tell him the Duke of Carabas owns this cornfield."
"I won't lie to the king," the man said.
Puss hissed and showed his claws.
Or I'll eat you for dinner!"
The man held up his hands. "Okay, okay!"
"That's a magnificent cornfield," the king said.
He was listening to the beautiful music.
The king leaned out of the carriage.
The king smiled when he heard the answer.
"I didn't know you owned a cornfield!"
Puss danced as he walked along.
"My plan is working perfectly!" he thought.
"An ogre owns it," the farmer said.
Puss puffed out his chest. "I'm not afraid of ogres!"
"You play the guitar so well, Fiona," Carabas said.
The king whispered in Fiona's ear.
He's rich and owns lots of land."
Fiona shrugged. "I want a husband who is kind."
He knocked on the castle's door.
"I'd like to speak with the ogre," Puss said.
"The ogre is out," the man said.
"You may come in and wait for him."
The man led Puss into a room.
The man called to a servant. "Bring us tea!"
His hand shook as he poured the tea.
"Why is the servant so nervous?" Puss thought.
"Thank you," Puss said to the man.
The man suddenly grew big and green.
The ogre stood in the doorway.
The ogre smiled, showing rotten teeth.
"I'll escape when I get a chance," he thought.
The ogre took a board from a shelf.
"If you win, I'll let you leave."
Puss and the ogre played checkers.
"When did you buy this castle?" Puss asked.
"I didn't buy it." The ogre chuckled.
The ogre was soon winning the game.
"I took a lot of his checkers," Puss thought.
"How does he still have so many?"
He saw something hidden in the ogre's hand.
He stood up and pointed at the ogre. "Cheater!"
"I'm not staying for lunch," Puss said.
"Yes, you are, Cat!" The ogre growled.
The ogre grabbed Puss and threw him into a cage.
The ogre carried the cage into the kitchen.
He slammed it onto the counter.
"Cook?" The ogre yelled for the cook.
So he began chopping onions himself.
"This lunch will be delicious," he said.
"I have to get out of here," Puss thought.
He tried to bend the cage's bars.
He pretended to cry. "Oh, poor me!
Now I'll never get to live with the princess!"
"My master is going to marry her."
Will you pay me if I let you go?"
The ogre shrugged. "I want more money."
Puss pretended to think for a moment.
The ogre unlocked the cage door.
He threw them at the ogre's face.
Puss didn't have time to stop.
He kept running toward the door.
Puss skidded to a stop. "Oh no!"
A mean lion blocked the door!
"That lion is really the ogre!" he thought.
"How do I get out of this castle?" he thought.
Puss ran around a corner and saw stairs.
Puss hurried into a small room.
Quickly he slipped out a window and hid.
"I smell you, Cat!" the lion said.
The lion's big head appeared in the window.
"I'll bet you can't make yourself bigger."
"Of course I can!" the lion yelled.
Bam! His head hit the window.
The lion was an ogre again.
He was moaning and rubbing his head.
"This is my chance to escape!" Puss thought.
He slipped back inside through the window.
He was almost at the door . . .
"I'm going to squash you!" the ogre growled.
"I can't pay you if you squash me."
The ogre thought for a moment.
"I'll put you down now," the ogre said.
"You won't try to escape again, will you?"
Puss held a paw over his heart.
"Of course not. You can trust me."
The ogre put Puss on the floor.
"I'm sorry I tricked you before," Puss said.
"I didn't believe you could make yourself bigger."
"I can do lots of amazing things."
Puss gave the ogre a doubtful look.
"You don't believe me?" the ogre asked.
Suddenly two servants ran into the room.
"You got rid of the ogre!" one said.
"You are our hero!" the other said.
He walked out of the room.
Other servants peeked out from doorways.
"Is the ogre really gone?" one asked.
But the ogre put them in the dungeon."
Puss went down to the dungeon.
"How can we ever repay you?" a servant asked.
"The king will be here soon," Puss said.
"He will ask who owns this castle.
Tell him the Duke of Carabas owns it."
He looked at a couple of servants.
"Comb your hair and tuck in your shirts!"
Soon the carriage rolled up to the castle.
"This is a fine-looking home," the king said.
Just then Fiona's eyes went wide. "It's Puss!"
Puss stood in front of the castle.
We don't live in this castle!"
The king and Fiona walked over.
"This is a fine castle, Duke," the king said.
"Everybody looks neat and tidy," he said.
"Let's go to the dining room," Puss said.
The king laughed. "This castle is so big, Duke.
You forgot where the dining room is!"
Puss led everyone down a hallway.
"You have a lovely home, Duke," Fiona said.
"Oh, it's, um, just a house," Carabas said.
Fiona smiled. "It's nice that you don't brag."
"I don't care about money, Father," Fiona said.
"I just want to marry a kind man."
A feast was waiting in the dining room.
"But I must tell everyone the truth."
Puss handed Carabas the bread basket.
Carabas gasped. "Puss, your paw is bleeding!"
"Oh, it's not a big deal, Master.
I cut myself earlier, but I'm fine."
Carabas jumped to his feet and bowed.
"Excuse us for a moment, please," he said.
Carabas carried Puss to a washroom.
"Master, this is silly," Puss said. "I'm fine."
Gently Carabas wrapped the bandage around Puss' paw.
Fiona smiled and turned to her father.
"That's what I was talking about, Father," she whispered.
Fiona and Carabas were having a picnic.
Fiona smiled. "I wrote that song for you."
"Fiona, will you marry me?" Carabas blurted out.
Puss' head popped out of a bush.
"No, Puss." Carabas held up a hand.
"Fiona, I'm not a duke," Carabas said.
I understand if you won't marry me now."
Fiona shook her head. "I'm glad you told me.
But I don't care if you're rich or poor.
Three weeks later there was a royal wedding.
"I'm so happy for Master," he thought.
A cat was looking at him.
Her eyes were big and bright.
"Um, hello!" Puss said. "I mean, um, thank you!"
The cat smiled. "Would you like to dance?"
Together they headed for the dance floor.
